correctness.rationale: Complete group averaging preserves the objective; the transposition-odd commutator Gram has an explicit (m+1)-dimensional basis and exactly calculated entries. Its scalar standard mode is always strictly below the top eigenvalue of the 2x2 trivial block. The uniform positive quadratic coefficient proves strong convexity and a unique attained optimizer. Crossing-slope analysis rigorously gives the two-term high-degree expansion. A standalone standard-library exact-rational checker reconstructed the full graph commutator and 89,685 assertions for n=5..10 and nine rational parameters; finite tests only corroborate the unrestricted analytical proof.

value.rationale: The adjacency–Dirac Connes distance along an edge is a natural automorphism-orbit invariant of all triangular graphs, not an arbitrary slice. A high-dimensional operator-norm supremum becomes an explicit unique one-dimensional algebraic solution, with a two-term sharp asymptotic and the structural avoided crossing that determines its subleading coefficient. Existing generic bounds do not yield this exact finite family or correction; disjoint-pair and weighted variants remain meaningful follow-up problems.
